current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens on a direct second-person prohibition, וְאַתָּ֞ה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בְּעַד הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.7.16, byte tier) — ‘ve-attah al-titpallel be'ad ha-am ha-zeh,’ ‘and you, do not pray for this people’ — turning the address from the people back to the prophet himself, a discourse-frame imperative distinct from the temple-gate proclamation before it. The forbidden intercession is grounded in the offerings to the “queen of the sky” described at 7.18, the women knead the dough, to make cakes to the queen of the sky (web:Jer.7.18), and the unit closes on the consequence clause לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה (oshb:Jer.7.20, byte tier) — ‘lachen koh amar Adonai YHWH,’ ‘therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh’ — which keeps the same divine speaker as the prohibition and is retained by its own consequence connective, lachen ('therefore'), rather than by a shared referent: the prohibition's own referent is הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה, 'this people' (oshb:Jer.7.16, byte tier), while the closing verse's is הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה, 'this place' (oshb:Jer.7.20, byte tier) -- a different noun, not a recurrence of the first. The place-noun is itself a catchword reaching back across this row's own front seam to וְלַ֨מָּק֔וֹם (oshb:Jer.7.14, byte tier), 'and to the place,' which argues cohesion with the material just before this unit rather than within it. oshb:Jer.7.20 is also the book's only koh-amar adonai-YHWH stack (sweep: 1 verse), a uniquely attested title site; under the ruled granularity a speech-formula onset cuts only with a change of frame owner, and the mouth does not change here, so the formula still marks emphasis rather than a fresh address.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens on a shift to feminine-singular imperative address, גָּזִּ֤י נִזְרֵךְ֙ וְֽהַשְׁלִ֔יכִי וּשְׂאִ֥י עַל שְׁפָיִ֖ם קִינָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.7.29, byte tier) — ‘gozi nizrekh vehashlikhi u-se'i al shefayim qinah,’ ‘cut off your hair, and throw it away, and take up a lamentation on the bare heights’ — commanding an unnamed feminine-singular addressee to mourn, grounded in the abominations named at 7.30-31. The recurring judgment formula at 7.32 (sweep: 15 verses, skeleton tier), לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.7.32, byte tier) — ‘lachen hineh yamim ba'im, ne'um YHWH,’ ‘therefore behold, the days come, says Yahweh’ — turns the Topheth renaming toward a burial shortage, “The dead bodies of this people will be food for the birds of the sky” (web:Jer.7.33), that the 8.1 scene continues without a fresh word-event or date frame: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֣יא נְאֻם יְהוָ֡ה (oshb:Jer.8.1, byte tier, a verse carrying its own ketiv/qere note) — ‘ba'et ha-hi, ne'um YHWH,’ ‘at that time, declares Yahweh’ — extends the same no-burial judgment to the exhumed bones of kings, priests, and prophets, “They will not be gathered or be buried. They will be like dung on the surface of the earth” (web:Jer.8.2). The row closes at 8.3 because 8.4 opens a fresh commission to the prophet with its own koh-amar formula.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: The Topheth judgment (7.30-34) and the bone-exhumation scene (8.1-3) could split at the chapter break, but both develop the same burial-denial threat opened by the mourning command, so the chapter division is not read as a unit boundary here.
current_row.literature_type_guess: deuteronomic prose sermon (mourning command and burial-denial judgment)
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate

Setumot bound the row at oshb:Jer.7.28, immediately before it, run through the row at oshb:Jer.7.31, and close it at oshb:Jer.8.3 (single-witness, WLC). Three paseq segs stand in this span, at oshb:Jer.7.34, oshb:Jer.8.1, and oshb:Jer.8.2 (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position claim).
